m: Om. I meditate on her whose seat is the lord of serpents, whose body-vine shines with a great garland of gems from the serpent's hood, who is radiant as the sun and illumined by three eyes, who holds a rosary, a pot, a skull-cup, and a water-lily, who wears the crescent moon as her crest, the supreme one
dwelling in the lap of the all-knowing Lord Bhairava: Padmavati. Om. The seer said:
Hearing the Goddess's words, that messenger, filled with indignation, went back and reported them in full to the king of the daityas.
When the king of the asuras heard that messenger's report, he grew angry and spoke to Dhumralochana, a lord among the daityas.
Dhumralochana, go at once, surrounded by your own army, and bring that wicked woman here by force, dragged by the hair and thrown into confusion.
If anyone else rises to protect her, slay him, whether he is a god, a yaksha, or a gandharva.
The seer said:
Commanded by him, the daitya Dhumralochana went quickly, surrounded by sixty thousand asuras.
Seeing the Goddess dwelling on the snow mountain, he called out loudly, Come to the presence of Shumbha and Nishumbha.
If you will not go now, of your own accord, to my master, then I will take you by force, dragged by the hair and thrown into confusion.
The Goddess said:
You were sent by the lord of the daityas, you are strong, and you are surrounded by an army. If you take me by force in this way, what can I do to you?
The seer said:
Addressed in this way, the asura Dhumralochana rushed at her. Ambika then reduced him to ashes with a mere humkara.
Then Ambika rained sharp arrows, and also spears and battle-axes, upon the great army of asuras, which had become enraged.
Then the lion, the Goddess's own mount, shook his mane in anger, roared a terrible roar, and fell upon the asura army.
He struck some daityas with a blow of his paw, others with his jaws, and still others he crushed underfoot. Thus he killed the great asuras.
The maned one tore open the bellies of some with his claws, and with a blow of his paw he struck the heads off others.
Others he left with arms and heads cut away. Shaking his mane, he also drank the blood from the bellies of still others.
In a moment that whole army was brought to destruction by that great being, the Goddess's exceedingly angry mount, the maned lion.
Hearing that the Goddess had slain the asura Dhumralochana, and that the lion had destroyed the entire army,
Shumbha, lord of the daityas, became furious, his lip trembling, and he gave orders to the two great asuras, Chanda and Munda.
Chanda, Munda, go there surrounded by large forces. Go, and bring her here at once.
Drag her by the hair, or bind her, if you have any doubt about the fight. Otherwise let all the asuras, with every weapon, strike her down.
When that wicked woman has been slain and the lion has been brought down, come back quickly, having seized Ambika and bound her.
